transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well... I guess I'm here because of my eating. I have these nights where I just... eat. And afterward, I'm just sitting there with all the crumbs and empty containers around me. It's... well, I feel so ashamed. Just disgusted with myself. It's gotten to where I can hardly even pray, or... or look folks at church in the eye the next morning.
After these episodes of eating, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise a lot to try to get rid of the calories or keep from gaining weight?
No... no, I don't do anything like that. I just... I just sit there with it.
During these eating episodes, do you feel like you can't stop eating or control what you're eating?

Yes... I suppose so. Once the house is quiet and I take that first bite... it's like my good sense just steps aside. I'll be telling myself, 'Belinda, stop now'... but my hands just keep reaching for more. I can't seem to stop.
Do these eating episodes usually happen at night, after you've already had dinner or late in the evening?
I... I'm not really sure. I don't keep track of the time, or... if it's always right after supper. I just haven't paid much mind to exactly when it starts.
Do these eating episodes usually happen in a short period of time, like within a couple of hours, or does the eating go on for most of the evening or night?

I suppose it's... it's usually pretty quick. Just in one sitting. I don't sit there all night doing it. On a bad night, I might start with a plate of leftover funeral casserole... and before I know it, I've eaten that, and... half a pan of brownies. Some biscuits. Whatever chicken salad is left in the fridge. It all just happens... right then.
Do these eating episodes cause you a lot of distress, or interfere with your daily life, like your work, relationships, or going to church?

Well... yes. It bothers me a great deal. I... I don't like to talk about it much, but... I've started telling the ladies I can't make it to our bridge nights as often. And I stepped back from helping in the church kitchen. I just... I worry too much that someone might notice things missing, or... or look at me and see how ashamed I am. It's just easier to stay home.
During these eating episodes, do you find yourself eating much more rapidly than usual?

I... yes. I suppose I do. I just... I stand there at the kitchen counter, and... well, I eat so fast I barely even taste what I'm having. The pound cake, the crackers... sometimes I realize I'm swallowing before I've even rightly chewed it. It's just... fast.
During these episodes, do you feel like you're not in control of yourself, like you're just going through the motions and can't stop even if you wanted to?

Well... yes. I suppose so. It's... it's hard to explain. Once I take that first bite, usually after the house is quiet... it's just like my good sense steps aside. I'll be standing there telling myself, 'Belinda, stop now,' but... my hands just keep reaching for more. I don't know how to stop it once it starts.
Do you often eat even when you're not hungry, or do these episodes usually happen when you're already full?
I... I don't rightly know. I haven't really thought about whether my stomach is empty or not when it happens. I just... I suppose I don't pay much attention to that part of it.
Do you find yourself eating until you feel uncomfortably full during these episodes?

I... yes. It gets to where... well, I keep going until my stomach is just tight. It gets sore under my nightgown, and... I usually have to go ease myself into the recliner in the living room. It just hurts too much to move around after that.

latest_inference.note: The patient meets the diagnostic criteria for binge eating disorder, which is classified under F50.81.
